title: Expect the variance
scenario: You approved a marketing paragraph yesterday. Today you paste the same request and get slightly different wording, even though you changed nothing.
task: What is the realistic expectation and fix?

options.text: The product is broken — identical requests must return identical text.
options.feedback: Identical output is not the design. Generation samples from probabilities; small shifts — even across runs — change the wording.

options.text: Wording varies by design; keep approved text saved and paste it whenever it must be edited or reused.
options.feedback: Yes — variance is normal; commitments are snapshots. The saved approved version is the source of truth.

options.text: Ask it to “output exactly what you said yesterday” and it will comply.
options.feedback: Nothing stores “yesterday” unless that conversation is still in context — and across sessions, it is not.

options.text: Lower the temperature to zero and every future run will be word-for-word identical.
options.feedback: Lower randomness makes output more stable, not frozen — and most products do not even expose the setting.

hints: What is the difference between drafting and committing?
explanation: Model output is a draft with variance: sampling, wording and context all shift the result. Draft freely, then snapshot anything you commit to — and stop expecting exact repeats from a new run.
